annotations.title: Which US state privacy laws do these numbers cross?

description: Does a US state consumer-privacy law bind this business? Give the annual gross revenue, how many residents of a state whose personal data is held, and whether personal data is sold, and each of 18 state privacy statutes comes back with whether those figures cross a threshold the statute's own quoted sentence states, the sentence, the citation and the page it was read from. Use this instead of comparing thresholds from memory or from a table: they are inconsistent between states, several are written in words rather than digits, Utah and Tennessee join theirs with AND rather than OR, and four states (Texas, Nebraska, Florida, Tennessee) get NO verdict because the figures their laws turn on are not in the sentence we hold. A threshold with no checked figure is refused by name with the reason, never answered as a 'no'. This says what the statute's words state about these numbers; it does not say a law applies or that a system is compliant. This tool is served both here and at https://referencesource.org/mcp/compliance and the answer is the same at either address — one handler, not two. The underlying records, every threshold with its statute's own quoted sentence, are at https://referencesource.org/state-data-privacy-applicability-thresholds/ and https://referencesource.org/data-breach-notification-clocks/.

annual_revenue_usd.description: Annual gross revenue in US dollars, e.g. 40000000. Omit it and any revenue threshold comes back need_more rather than a guess.

sells_personal_data.description: Does the business sell or share personal data for money or other valuable consideration? Several states have a lower resident threshold that only applies if it does.

share_of_revenue_from_selling_pct.description: What percentage of gross revenue comes from selling personal data, e.g. 30 for 30%. Needed only for the states whose quoted sentence states a percentage (25%, 20% or 50%).

state_residents.description: How many residents OF THE STATE being asked about whose personal data the business holds (bought, sold, shared or processed, as each statute defines it). One figure is applied to every state asked for, so call once per state where the counts differ.

states.description: Optional. The states to answer for, as the printed name ("New Jersey") or the id ("new-jersey"). Omit it for every state in the table, which is usually the question. A name matching nothing is reported back in states_not_recognised, never dropped — our table not holding a state is not the same fact as that state having no such law.

name: which_state_privacy_laws_apply

record_url.description: This record's own page on referencesource.org.

source_quote.description: Verbatim text from that page containing the threshold or the deadline.

source_url.description: The statute page the words were read from.

verdict.description: crosses | below | on_the_line | need_more | no_verdict. on_the_line means a figure sits exactly on a boundary the statute does not fix; need_more means a number this statute turns on was not given; no_verdict means this state's own thresholds are not figures our records hold.
